note: Primary fixture alias for #92510. On macOS Apple Silicon, the Apple Virtualization VM that Cowork/Code launches accumulates host-side open file descriptors continuously, including while completely idle. Faceplate: saturating.
version: Claude Desktop (Cowork/Code VM), current release as of 2026-09-06 — not the CLI
title: [BUG] Cowork/Code VM leaks host file descriptors (~400k) until macOS exhausts kern.maxfiles and panics/reboots
expected: The VM should release host file descriptors when the guest closes files and when a session ends, keeping the fd count bounded. An idle VM should not grow its fd usage, and the app should never be able to push the host past kern.maxfiles.
actual: Host VM process holds ~409,600 fds (~71% of kern.maxfiles, ~130x next-largest). Guest /proc/sys/fs/file-nr → 512. Count climbs while idle, including 12h after last prompt. Exhaustion → macOS kernel panic → reboot.
pressureSnapshot: Claude-owned Apple Virtualization VM: ~409,600 open file descriptors (~71% of kern.maxfiles, ~130x next-largest process)
Codex/Node (hundreds of processes): ~106,000 fds in an earlier snapshot (secondary)
Inside the VM (guest) at boot: /proc/sys/fs/file-nr -> 512 0 ... ; 5 processes; top process holds 4 fds; uptime 2 min
Outcome: system-wide fd exhaustion -> macOS kernel panic -> reboot
watch: sudo lsof -n | awk '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -5
workarounds: kill the VM PID (Claude relaunches it on next use)
coalition: Associated with Claude, not Docker. Codex/Node were a secondary contributor, not the dominant holder.
additional: Claude session start times match the VM's launch time, and Claude died during the final collapse.
Multiple Cowork sessions may have the same folder connected concurrently.
Existing VM reports (#26087, #47829, #26646, #65239, #47644) cover guest kernel panics and disk-write limits, not host fd exhaustion.
Claude Code run from Terminal (no VM) does not exhibit this.
hypothesisNonBinding: Most likely the virtiofs / shared-folder layer not releasing host handles for files the guest has touched. Verify nothing — encode the issue body only. Do not invent source-code claims.
